syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: How macroeconomics differs from microeconomics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why macroeconomics can study the whole economy through aggregate variables and a single representative good.
Distinguish microeconomic questions and agents from macroeconomic ones.
Explain why macroeconomics sometimes divides the economy into a few distinct goods or sectors.

topics.title: Economic agents and why macroeconomics is needed

concepts.learning_objective: Define economic agents and identify consumers, producers and institutions as examples.
State the reasons economists had to look beyond Adam Smith's self-interest view of markets.
Identify macroeconomic decision-makers such as the State, RBI and SEBI and the public goals they pursue.

topics.title: Emergence of macroeconomics

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the classical view of full employment that dominated economics before Keynes.
Describe the Great Depression of 1929 and calculate the unemployment rate from its definition.
Explain how Keynes's General Theory (1936) gave rise to macroeconomics as a separate branch.

topics.title: The capitalist economy and its firms

concepts.learning_objective: State the features of a capitalist economy and recognise economies to which they do not apply.
Match the factors of production with rent, interest, wages and profit.
Identify investment expenditure as spending that raises productive capacity.

topics.title: Four sectors of the economy

concepts.learning_objective: Define a household and explain how households earn incomes and support firms' markets.
Describe the economic functions of the government sector.
Explain exports, imports and capital flows as links with the external sector.

topics.title: Some basic concepts of macroeconomics

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish final goods (consumption and capital goods, consumer durables) from intermediate goods by their economic use.
Distinguish stock variables, defined at a point of time, from flow variables, defined over a period of time.
Relate gross investment, depreciation and net investment, and explain the time trade-off between capital and consumer goods.

topics.title: Circular flow of income

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four factors of production and their remunerations: wage, interest, profit and rent.
Explain the circular flow of income and goods between households and firms in a simple economy.
Explain why the product, expenditure and income methods measure the same aggregate at different points of the circular flow.

topics.title: The product or value added method

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate value added and explain how deducting intermediate goods avoids double counting.
Calculate gross and net value added, using change in inventories and depreciation.
Distinguish inventory (a stock) from change in inventories (a flow), and planned from unplanned changes.

topics.title: Expenditure method and income method

concepts.learning_objective: Compute GDP as C + I + G + X - M and explain the treatment of intermediate goods and imports.
Compute GDP as the sum of wages, profits, interest and rent, and verify it against value added.

topics.title: Factor cost, basic prices and market prices

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish production taxes and subsidies from product taxes and subsidies with examples.
Convert GVA between factor cost, basic prices and market prices using net production and net product taxes.

topics.title: Some macroeconomic identities

concepts.learning_objective: Derive GNP, NNP at market prices and National Income (NNP at factor cost) from GDP.
Derive Personal Income and Personal Disposable Income from National Income.
Calculate National Disposable Income and identify the components of Private Income.

topics.title: Nominal and real GDP and price indices

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish nominal GDP at current prices from real GDP at constant base-year prices.
Calculate the GDP (or GNP) deflator and interpret what it says about the price level.
Calculate a Consumer Price Index and explain how CPI and WPI differ from the GDP deflator.

topics.title: GDP and welfare

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate why a rise in GDP may not raise welfare when its distribution is unequal.
Explain how non-monetary exchanges lead to underestimation of GDP.
Explain how negative and positive externalities make GDP misstate welfare.

topics.title: Barter exchange and the functions of money

concepts.learning_objective: Explain barter exchange and why the double coincidence of wants makes it costly in a large economy.
Describe money as a medium of exchange and a unit of account and use it to work out relative prices.
Explain money as a store of value and how a rising price level erodes its purchasing power.

topics.title: Demand for money: income, interest and the transaction motive

concepts.learning_objective: State how the demand for money depends on income and on the rate of interest.
Calculate and interpret the transaction demand for money using MdT = kT and MdT = kPY.
Calculate the velocity of circulation of money and relate it to k.

topics.title: Speculative demand for money, bond prices and the liquidity trap

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using present value, why the price of a bond is inversely related to the market rate of interest.
Explain why the speculative demand for money is inversely related to the rate of interest.
Describe the liquidity trap and why extra money then fails to lower the rate of interest.

topics.title: Central bank and commercial banks

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the functions of the central bank and the meaning of high-powered money.
Explain how commercial banks accept deposits, lend part of them and earn the spread, as in Lala's story.

topics.title: Money creation by the banking system and the money multiplier

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the assets, liabilities and net worth of a bank's balance sheet.
Explain how the Cash Reserve Ratio limits the loans a bank can make in each round.
Calculate the money multiplier and the deposits and loans created from a given amount of reserves.

topics.title: Policy tools to control money supply

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the central bank is called the lender of last resort.
Distinguish quantitative and qualitative tools of monetary control and the effect of the bank rate.
Explain outright open market operations, repo and reverse repo and their effect on money supply.

topics.title: Measures of money supply, fiat money and demonetisation
topics.ncert_sections: The supply of money: various measures; Box 3.2

concepts.learning_objective: Define fiat money and legal tender and explain why demand deposits are not legal tender.
State and calculate M1, M2, M3 and M4 and rank them by liquidity.
Evaluate the effects of the 2016 demonetisation on the economy and the banking system.

topics.title: Ex ante and ex post measures

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish planned (ex ante) values of macroeconomic variables from their actual (ex post) values.
Calculate ex post investment from planned investment and unplanned changes in inventories.

topics.title: Consumption function, MPC and MPS

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the consumption function C = C-bar + cY with its autonomous and induced parts.
State and apply the relation MPC + MPS = 1 and the possible values of MPC.
Compute the average propensities to consume and to save at a given income.

topics.title: Investment and aggregate demand in the two-sector model

concepts.learning_objective: Define investment and explain why it is treated as autonomous in the simple model.
Express ex ante aggregate demand as the sum of consumption, investment and, with government, G - cT.
Explain how unplanned inventory changes reconcile planned output with planned demand.

topics.title: Equilibrium income with a fixed price level

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the price level is assumed fixed at the first stage of macroeconomic analysis.
Interpret the 45-degree line diagram to locate equilibrium and disequilibrium positions.
Calculate equilibrium income using Y = (C-bar + I)/(1 - c) and test whether an economy is in equilibrium.

topics.title: Autonomous changes and the multiplier

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a change in autonomous expenditure shifts the aggregate demand line.
Calculate the investment multiplier 1/(1 - c) and the resulting change in equilibrium income.
Trace the round-by-round working of the multiplier process.

topics.title: Paradox of thrift

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why an increase in the propensity to save leaves total savings unchanged or lower.
Distinguish a swing of the AD line caused by a change in MPC from a parallel shift.

topics.title: Full employment, deficient and excess demand

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why equilibrium income need not be the full employment level of income.
Identify situations of deficient and excess demand and their long-run effect on prices.
State the effective demand principle under a fixed price and perfectly elastic supply.

topics.title: Government budget: meaning and objectives

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the constitutional basis of the budget and why it is split into revenue and capital accounts.
Distinguish public goods from private goods using non-rivalry and non-excludability, and public provision from public production.
Identify the allocation, redistribution and stabilisation functions of the government budget.

topics.title: Classification of receipts

concepts.learning_objective: Classify revenue receipts into tax and non-tax revenue and describe progressive and proportional taxation.
Identify capital receipts as those that create liabilities or reduce financial assets, debt creating or non-debt creating.

topics.title: Classification of expenditure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify revenue expenditure and its main items such as interest, defence, subsidies, salaries and grants.
Identify capital expenditure as spending that creates assets or reduces financial liabilities.
State the purpose of the three fiscal policy statements laid with the budget under the FRBMA.

topics.title: Balanced, surplus and deficit budgets; measures of deficit

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish balanced, surplus and deficit budgets.
Compute the revenue deficit and interpret its implications for government dissaving.
Compute fiscal and primary deficits and interpret them as measures of borrowing requirement.

topics.title: Fiscal policy and the multipliers

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the government expenditure multiplier and the change in equilibrium income with lump-sum taxes.
Calculate and compare the tax, transfer and balanced budget multipliers.
Analyse how proportional taxes reduce the multiplier and act as automatic stabilisers.

topics.title: Government debt, deficit reduction, FRBMA and GST

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate perspectives on the burden of debt, including Ricardian equivalence and crowding out.
Explain ways of reducing deficits and the main features of the FRBMA, 2003.
Explain how GST works as a destination-based value-added tax that removes cascading.

topics.title: Open economy, its linkages and foreign trade

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the output, financial and labour market linkages through which an open economy interacts with other countries.
Explain how imports act as a leakage and exports as an injection in the circular flow of income.
Explain why a national currency is accepted internationally only when it keeps a stable purchasing power.

topics.title: Balance of payments and the current account

concepts.learning_objective: Define the balance of payments and identify its main accounts.
Classify trade in goods, services and transfer payments as components of the current account.
Distinguish between balance of trade and current account balance and calculate both from given data.

topics.title: Capital account and BoP surplus or deficit

concepts.learning_objective: Identify credit and debit items of the capital account such as FDI, FII, borrowings and assistance.
Calculate the overall balance of payments and explain how official reserve transactions settle a deficit or surplus.
Distinguish between autonomous (above the line) and accommodating (below the line) transactions.

topics.title: The foreign exchange market and the exchange rate

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the foreign exchange market, its participants and the meaning of the foreign exchange rate.
Explain the sources of demand for and supply of foreign exchange and how they respond to the exchange rate.

topics.title: Flexible exchange rate and its determinants

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a flexible exchange rate is determined and distinguish depreciation from appreciation.
Analyse how speculation, interest rate differentials and income changes affect the exchange rate in the short run.
Apply the purchasing power parity theory to predict long-run exchange rates.

topics.title: Fixed exchange rates and managed floating

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a government maintains a fixed exchange rate and distinguish devaluation from revaluation.
Evaluate the merits and demerits of fixed and flexible exchange rate systems, including speculative attacks.
Describe managed floating as a mix of a flexible rate and central bank intervention.

topics.title: Determination of equilibrium income in an open economy

concepts.learning_objective: State the national income identity for an open economy and interpret net exports.
Identify the marginal propensity to import from an import function and explain its role in aggregate demand.
Calculate the open economy multiplier and explain why it is smaller than the closed economy multiplier.
